findings.text: Public predicate reports whether secretmem is in use by inspecting a global file count. A nonzero count means active and zero means idle.
Global address space operations for secretmem describe dirty, free and migrate behavior shared by all secretmem mappings.
Helper reports swapped bytes for an address space subrange by scanning the page cache for swap values.
Helper reports swapped bytes for a virtual area, using a cached total for whole-file mappings and a range scan otherwise.
Helper clears unevictable marking from all folios in a mapping unless the mapping becomes unevictable concurrently.
Per-inode secretmem state pairs an owning user reference with a signed tally of pages currently charged to that user.
Fallocate progress record holds a wait queue for faulters plus start, next, newly allocated and unswapped counts as page offsets.
Mount option record holds block and inode limits, NUMA policy, ownership, mode, full inode numbers flag, huge mode, seen mask, swap and quota settings, plus optional unicode decoding state.

Charging pages against a user succeeds immediately for zero length, otherwise enforces a memlock-derived page ceiling with a compare exchange loop on the user locked total, and on success also bumps the per-inode tally.
Uncharging subtracts the same page count from both the user locked total and the per-inode tally, and the bulk variant uncharges whatever the per-inode tally currently holds.
Faults beyond current file size fail as invalid, otherwise the handler holds a shared invalidation lock across cache lookup and potential installation.
New secretmem files start as zero-length regular files with user-charged unevictable mappings, private state owned by the creator, and a global user count increment.
File release decrements the global user count and destroys private state by uncharging all pages, dropping the user reference and clearing the inode pointer.
Mapping preparation only allows shared mappings, marks the area as non-dumpable, and installs the secretmem fault handler.
Secretmem folios never migrate, freeing restores the direct map and wipes content, and dirtying is a no-op.
Attribute changes take an exclusive invalidation lock and reject size changes once a nonzero size exists, otherwise delegating to the simple helper.
Default tmpfs limits derive from total RAM with half the pages for blocks and the minimum of low memory, half the pages and a large constant divided by inode size for inodes.
Size re-accounting is skipped when the no-reserve flag is set, otherwise it charges the growth or uncharges the shrink through memory accounting helpers.
Cache entry replacement requires expected and replacement to be present, fails when the current entry differs, and otherwise stores the replacement.
Huge option parsing accepts six textual names, rejects modes needing hugepage support when absent, and rejects forced PMD mode unless the inherit mask selects only PMD order.
Huge option formatting provides the inverse name for each numeric mode and treats unknown values as a bug returning a sentinel word.
Unused huge shrink scan stops when the per-superblock list is empty, and its count helper returns zero for non-root memory cgroup reclaim.
Removal from cache atomically swaps a folio for a swap value, detaches the folio from its mapping, adjusts page and statistics counts, and drops references while asserting replacement success.
Swap freeing only clears an entry exactly matching the expected value and fully contained in the requested range, releasing the corresponding swap slots.
Range swap accounting walks the cache under read-side protection, counts value entries scaled by their order, cooperates with scheduling, and reports bytes.

Range undo converts byte bounds to page indices with saturation for maximal end, clamps an in-progress fallocate end, and treats swap and resident entries differently when unwinding a failed fallocate.
Secretmem faulting uses a shared invalidation lock while attribute changes use the exclusive form, both held across cache and size operations and released on all exits.
Shmem cache mutation holds interrupt-disabled xarray locks, swap usage scans use read-side critical sections with periodic rescheduling, and swap list updates serialize on a dedicated spinlock.

Fault handling proceeds from size validation to shared locking to locked lookup, then on miss through zeroed allocation, user charging, direct map invalidation, uptodate marking, cache insertion with retry on races, TLB flushing, and finally returns a locked page.

Secretmem filesystem setup mounts only when enabled and direct map control exists, while file creation flows from secure inode allocation through private state init to pseudo file wiring and user count increment with cleanup on each failure.

Undo passes from locked entry processing to edge partial handling and then whole folio reclamation, skipping partial work for failed fallocate unwinding and restarting or repositioning when entries change concurrently.
Secret file system call gates on enablement and direct map capability, validates flag masks and user count bounds, then creates a secret file and installs it as a descriptor.
Operation tables connect secretmem release and mapping preparation, page fault handling, attribute setting, and address space dirty free and migrate handling.
Quota helpers enable per-type tracking with usage and limits, disable all types, and expose per-inode quota references.

Allocation failures must unwind charging and restore the direct map before dropping the folio, avoiding leaks and leaving kernel mappings restricted only after successful insertion plus TLB maintenance.

Truncation and fallocate races are contained by revalidating folio ownership after locking, retrying cache insertion conflicts, and skipping large swap entries that straddle range edges after edge zeroing.
Directory entry estimate is twenty, inode estimate is one thousand twenty four, short symlink threshold is one hundred twenty eight, and inode batch size is one thousand twenty four.
Huge modes are never zero always one within size two advise three deny minus one force minus two, and option seen bits are blocks one inodes two huge four inums eight quota sixteen.
Secretmem uses a dedicated filesystem name and anon inode label plus a pseudo file label, created read write with large file support.

Default huge policy for shmem and tmpfs each resolves at build time to one numeric huge mode held in read-mostly storage, alongside separate order masks for always madvise inherit and within size plus a configured flag, with a fallback that pins the effective mode to deny when hugepage support is unavailable.

Shmem core interfaces are forward declared for later definition, covering superblock handling, address space handling, file handling, three inode variants, two virtual memory variants and filesystem registration.
Secretmem and shmem each retain a global mount pointer for their pseudo filesystem, with the shmem pointer marked read-only after initialization.
